items.item: settings.json test write: read by the other host and kept by its writer
items.detail: the test write uses Pi's own procedure (proper-lockfile lock, migrate, merge modified fields, 2-space rewrite); the other host then reads the file and writes it with `install <local package>`

each host's own settings writer ran over a tree written by each host and kept every tracked key: fork-writes-fork-tree {"ok":true,"removed":[],"changed":[],"added":["packages"]}, official-writes-fork-tree {"ok":true,"removed":[],"changed":[],"added":[]}, official-writes-managed-tree {"ok":true,"removed":[],"changed":[],"added":["packages"]}, fork-writes-managed-tree {"ok":true,"removed":[],"changed":[],"added":[]}
pi writes auth.json only from the interactive `/login` flow; the RPC protocol and the extension API expose no credential write, so no headless product write path exists
neither host wrote models.json during any phase; the file is user-authored and no headless product write path was observed
observed but not exercised
project trust is granted interactively; no phase created or changed trust.json

each host writes only its own version directory and leaves the other's byte-identical (fork=["0.6.0"], bundle=["0.1.0"]). Neither host reads the other's version directory, so a leftover tree is inert rather than wrong.
/home/betiz/.spirits/agent kept its content and modification times across every phase (sessions/ excluded: this runner's own session transcript lives there)
